case_name: Kuncham Venkannan And 8 Others vs The State Of Telangana And Another

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Kuncham Venkannan and 8 others (husband, wife, etc.)
parties.respondent_defendant: The State of Telangana and another (wife, complainant, etc.)

facts_of_case: Petitioners filed a petition to quash the FIR registered for an offence punishable under Section 494 r/w 34 IPC. The contention is that there was a decree of divorce in O.P.No.1743 of 2015 on 09.04.2017, and the so-called second marriage between petitioners 1 and 2 was performed on 10.07.2017.

legal_principles.principle: After expiry of the appeal time from a decree of divorce, where an appeal is not presented or an appeal presented but dismissed, it shall be lawful for either party to the marriage to marry again.
legal_principles.held: Though from the very wording of Section 15 of the Act and the analogy taken, once there is an ex parte set aside application filed by the 2nd respondent, admittedly, by the time the so called second marriage between petitioners 1 and 2 performed on 10.07.2017, the analogy of pending appeal equally applies to the pending application.
cited_cases: Denny Pazhoor v. Greeta Sunitha Vincent, (Year) X SCC Y

legal_principles.principle: Mere filing of an appeal is not sufficient; there must be a stay equally.
legal_principles.held: Once there is an ex parte decree set aside application without even stated pending, he could not have been undergone the so called ceremony of marriage.
cited_cases: Denny Pazhoor v. Greeta Sunitha Vincent, (Year) X SCC Y

outcome.final_order: The Criminal Petition is disposed of. All defences of the petitioners are left open.

keywords: Denny Pazhoor v. Greeta Sunitha Vincent
